questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not an insectivorous plant?
questions.solution: Monotropa is a saprophytic plant, whereas Nepenthes, Sarracenia, Drosera, Dionaea, and Utricularia are insectivorous plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The most important role of K<sup>+</sup> ions is that
options: It influences many enzymic activities which regulate many plant processes.
It helps in the formation of cambium.
questions.solution: Potassium acts as an activator of several enzymes including DNA polymerase. It is an activator of more than 40 enzymes which regulates many plant processes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A free-living nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium which can also form a symbiotic association with the water fern Azolla is
questions.solution: The freshwater fern Azolla harbors Anabaena (a blue-green alga) in its leaf cavities. Chlorella is simply a green alga. Nostoc and Tolypothrix are a free-living cyanobacterium involved in N2 fixation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which element is required for the germination of pollen grains?
questions.solution: Boron is the micronutrient for plants, present in the soil in very small amounts. It is absorbed from the soil in the form of boric acid (<math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math>) and tetraborate anions. Boron is required for pollen germination, seed germination and cell differentiation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a bacterium involved in denitrification?
questions.solution: Some bacteria such as Thiobacillus denitrificans, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Micrococcus denitrificans also occur in the soil which converts the nitrate and ammonia into atmospheric free elemental nitrogen. Such bacteria are called denitrifying bacteria and the process is called denitrification. These bacteria act very well in the soil where there are more water and less oxygen and there is a high level of the carbohydrate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following elements is not an essential micronutrient for plant growth?
questions.solution: Essential microelements are Fe, Mn, Zn, B, Cu, and Mo. Essential macronutrients are C, H, N, P, S, Ca, K, and Mg.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following species does not have the ability to fix atmospheric nitrogen?
questions.solution: Nitrogen fixation is carried by prokaryotic cells, bacteria and cyanobacteria having Nif gene. Nif gene produces an enzyme nitrogenase which carries out nitrogen fixation. Spirogyra is a green algae that lacks nif gene thus cannot carry out nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Essential elements are
options: Required only in those metabolic processes responsible for biomass growth.
questions.solution:
The criteria for the essentiality of an element are given below:

(i) The element must be absolutely necessary for supporting normal growth and reproduction. In the absence of the element the plants do not complete their life cycle or set the seeds.

(ii) The requirement of the element must be specific and not replaceable by another element. In other words, deficiency of any one element cannot be met by supplying some other element.

(iii) The element must be directly involved in the metabolism of the plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If plant material is dried and burnt in a crucible, the residue would contain
options: Oxides and carbonates of about ten elements
Oxides and carbonates of Ca and Mg only
questions.solution: If dried plant parts are heated in silica crucible at 600°C all organic substances vaporize and the remaining plant ash contains only inorganic substances or essential mineral elements. The essential elements are C, H. O, N, P, K, S, Mg, Ca, Fe, Mo, Mn, Ni, Zn, B, Cl, Cu.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A mineral deficiency is likely to affect older leaves more than younger leaves if
options: The mineral is very mobile within the plant
The mineral is required for chlorophyll synthesis
The deficiency persists for a short time
questions.solution: Rapid remobilization of minerals creates deficiency first in the older leaves. So older leaves are first to show the deficiency of rapidly remobilized elements.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The deficiency of micronutrients, not only affect the growth of a plant but also affects the vital functions such as photosynthesis and cellular respiration. Among the list given below, which group of three elements shall affect both photosynthesis and cellular respiration the most?
questions.solution:
Copper deficiency usually results in shriveling or malformation of the leaves along with tip burn. The most easily recognized symptoms of copper deficiency are those in a disease of fruit trees called "exanthema".

Magnesium plays two very essential roles in the processes of photosynthesis and carbohydrate metabolism. Magnesium deficiencies show up as extensive chlorosis between the veins of the leaves. Chlorosis is followed by the appearance of anthocyanin pigments in the leaves such as the oranges, reds, and purples.

Iron functions in the synthesis of chloroplastic protein and thus may interfere with chlorophyll synthesis. Iron deficiencies of plant leaves appear as extensive chlorosis in the foliage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a macronutrient?
questions.solution: Macronutrients (macro-elements or major-elements) are required by plants in larger amounts (generally present in the plant tissues in concentrations of 1 to 10mg/gram of dry matter). Carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorous, potassium, calcium, sulfur, and magnesium are the nine macroelements in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Conversion of <math><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> is called ______ and is catalysed by______
options: Nitrate assimilation, nitrate and nitrite reductase
questions.solution: Plant absorbs nitate from soil but cannot utilize it, and it gets converted to ammonium ion for formation of amino acid. This process is known as nitrate assimilation and is catalysed by enzyme nitrate and nitrite reductase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The conversion of <math><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> to <math><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> occurs in
questions.solution: Reactions throughout the course of the nitrate assimilation pathway occur in separate cells and cellular compartments; nitrate is first transferred from root epidermal cells to the cytosol of leaf cells via vascular tissues, and the subsequently reduced nitrogen species move, also via vascular tissues, from chloroplasts to sink organs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following organisms has a role in converting ammonia into nitrites?
questions.solution:
Ammonia is converted into nitrate by nitrifying activities of bacteria, this process is called nitrification. Soil bacteria such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrosococcus convert ammonia to nitrite.

NH3+3O2 →2HNO2+2H2O

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is a micronutrient for plants?
questions.solution: Nutrients which are required in large amounts and functioning of the plant are known as macronutrients eg. Ca, Mg, N. Nutrients required in trace amounts are known as micronutrients. Manganese is a micronutrient for plants essential for the synthesis of chlorophyll. It is also required for activation of enzymes of respiration and nitrogen metabolism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During ionic flux, uptake of ions into inner space is
questions.solution: The movement of ions is called flux. The movement of ions into the cell is called influx and outward migration of ions is known as efflux. The energy is considered to be involved in the transport of such free ions across the membrane. The absorption of ions, involving the use of metabolic energy, is called active absorption. Energy used in these mechanisms comes from metabolic activities. Mineral absorption is mainly an active process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plants can be cultivated in soil less medium where all required nutrients are supplied from the outside in water solution, this method comes under
questions.solution: In 1860, Julius von Sachs, a prominent German botanist, demonstrated, for the first time, that plants could be grown to maturity in a defined nutrient solution in the complete absence of soil. This technique of growing plants in a nutrient solution is known as hydroponics.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a micronutrient?
questions.solution: Magnesium is a macronutrient. Micronutrients are essential elements that are required by plants in a small amount. They include Fe, Cu, B, Mo, Mn, Cl, and Ni. Macronutrients, on the other hand, are those essential elements that are required by plants in a larger amount. The examples include C, H, 0, N, S, P, K, Ca, and Mg.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A plant requires magnesium for
questions.solution: Plants require magnesium for chlorophyll synthesis. All four tetrapyrrole rings bind with magnesium (Mg++) ion at the center of chlorophyll molecule.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the correctly matched ones from the following.

I. Nitrosomonas - Nitrite to nitrate
II. Thiobacillus - Denitrification
III. Nostoc - Free-living nitrogen-fixer
IV. Azotobacter - Anaerobic nitrogen-fixer
questions.solution:
Nitrate present in the soil is reduced to nitrogen by the process of denitrification. Denitrification is carried by bacteria Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus.
A number of cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc are free-living nitrogen-fixers.
Azotobacter and Beijernickia are free-living nitrogen-fixing aerobic microbes.
Nitrosomonas and/or Nitrosococcus oxidise NH3 to nitrite.
The nitrite is further oxidised to nitrate with the help of Nitrobacter and Nitrocystis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Excess of manganese induces a deficiency of
questions.solution: Manganese competes with iron and magnesium for uptake and with magnesium for binding with the enzyme. Excess of manganese may induce deficiencies of iron, magnesium, and calcium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In root nodules of leguminous plants, the function of leg-hemoglobin during biological nitrogen fixation is
questions.solution: Leghemoglobin is an oxygen-carrying protein, somewhat similar to the hemoglobin of blood, that helps maintain the low oxygen tension necessary for effective nitrogen fixation. This is an essential component for nitrogen fixation by legumes. Leghemoglobin is produced as a result of symbiotic association between bacteroid and plant. The major role of leghemoglobin involves protection of nitrogenase enzyme from denaturation, if exposed to atmospheric concentration of oxygen, but at the same time supply of ample amount of oxygen to bacteria for respiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which amino acid plays a central role in nitrogen metabolism?
questions.solution: Glutamic acid is the first amino acid to be synthesized in nitrogen metabolism by the reamination of <math><mi>α</mi></math> -ketoglutaric acid from which 17 different amino acids are synthesized by transanimation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following plants have an association with Rhizobium?
[Sweet pea, Lentils, Garden pea, Alfalfa, Alnus, Frankia, Soybean, Clover beans]
questions.solution:
Alnus and Frankia are not associated with the legume family, rest all are legume plants. Legume plants show symbiotic association with Rhizobium.
Rhizobium is a bacterial genus associated with the formation of root nodules in plants of the legume family. These are symbiotic bacteria which take in nitrogen from the atmosphere and pass it on to the plant, allowing it to grow in soil low in nitrogen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not caused by the deficiency of minerals?
questions.solution: Etiolation is the symptom developed in plants when grown in the dark. Examples include pale yellow or white colour due to lack of chlorophyll, long internodes, small and rudimentary leaves, poor development of significant tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect pair from the following.
questions.solution: Phloem transport is carried out by boron and potassium. Boron regulates the translocation of solutes thus regulates the pressure gradient of the sieve tube element of phloem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One of the free-living, anaerobic nitrogen-fixer is:
questions.solution: Rhodospirillum is a free-living, anaerobic nitrogen fixer bacteria. It can synthesize its food in presence of light under anaerobic condition. Beijernickia and Azotobacter are free living aerobic nitrogen fixing bacteria. Rhizobium is a symbiotic nitrogen fixing bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The conversion of nitrate to nitrogen is called
questions.solution: Denitrification is the reduction of nitrate to gaseous compounds of nitrogen. Under anaerobic conditions, some microorganisms use nitrate and other oxidized ions as a source of oxygen, e.g., Pseudomonas denitrificans, Thiobacillus denitrificans, Micrococcus denitrificans, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Yellowing of tea leaf is due to the deficiency of
questions.solution: Chlorosis is the loss of chlorophyll leading to yellowing in leaves. This symptom is caused by the deficiency of elements N, K, Mg, S, Fe, Mn, Zn, and Mo. The tea yellow disease is caused by a sulphur deficiency in tea plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The deficiencies of micronutrients, not only affect the growth of plants but also vital functions such as photosynthetic and mitochondrial electron flow. Among the list given below, which group of three elements shall affect most, both photosynthetic and mitochondrial electron transport?
questions.solution: Iron is mainly available in the ferrous form and it is absorbed in the ferric form, also. It is a part of catalases, peroxidases, cytochromes etc. and plays a role in the electron transport system in photosynthesis. Manganese is absorbed by the plants when it is in the bivalent form. Manganese participates in the photolysis of water in photosystem II during photosynthesis and thus it helps in the electron transport of water to chlorophyll. Copper is absorbed on the clay particles as divalent cations, from where it can be absorbed by the plants by exchange mechanism. It is constituent of plastocyanin which takes part in electron transport during photosynthetic phosphorylation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Coralloid roots of Cycas are useful in
questions.solution: Anabaena, Nostoc and other cyanobacteria are found in coralloid roots hence it helps in fixation/absorption of nitrogen. The coralloid roots containing these symbiotic cyanobacteria (blue-green algae), apart from fixing nitrogen produce beneficial amino acids asparagine and citrulline.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Below diagram showing a technique for the culture of plants. This technique has been successfully employed for the production of which of the following?
questions.solution: The above diagram shows the hydroponic technique. Hydroponics is a subset of hydroculture and is a method of growing plants using mineral nutrient solutions, in water, without soil. This technique has been successfully employed for the production of seedless cucumber, lettuce and tomato plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In nitrogen cycle, which of the following plays an important role?
questions.solution: Nitrobacter is an N2 fixing organism, it fixes atmospheric free N2 into soluble salts like nitrites and nitrates. The fixed N2 is absorbed by plants, the N2 flows on the carnivores through the food chain. Hence, it is important for the N2 cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many protons and electrons are required to fix a dinitrogen?
questions.solution:
In nitrogen-fixing microorganisms, the eight high-potential electrons come from reduced ferredoxin, generated by photosynthesis or oxidative processes. Two molecules of ATP are hydrolyzed for each electron transferred. Thus, at least 16 molecules of ATP are hydrolyzed for each molecule of N2 reduced. 8 protons are needed for this reduction.

N2 + 8 e- + 8 H+ + 16 ATP → 2 NH3 + H2 + 16 ADP + 16 iP

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chlorosis is caused due to the deficiency of
questions.solution: Magnesium is a component of chlorophyll and an important binding substance for ribosomal sub-units. Its deficiency causes inter-veinal chlorosis, development of anthocyanin and depression of internal phloem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The process of conversion of organic nitrogen from dead material to ammonia is known as
questions.solution: Ammonification is the process by which the organically bound nitrogen of microbial, plant, and animal biomass is recycled after their death. Ammonification is carried out by a diverse array of microorganisms that perform ecological decay services and its product is ammonia or ammonium ion

questions.q:

 (B) Sulphur  (2) Not important for plants
 (C) Iodine  (3) Structural component of chlorophyll
 (D) Manganese  (4) Component of sugar
   (5) Required for enzyme activity
questions.solution:

 Sulphur  Found in some amino acid

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Manganese toxicity causes:
options: Reduces uptake of magnesium and iron
questions.solution: The prominent symptom of manganese toxicity is the appearance of brown spots surrounded by chlorotic veins. Manganese competes with iron and magnesium for uptake and with magnesium for binding with enzymes. Manganese also inhibits calcium translocation in the shoot apex. Therefore, excess of manganese may, in fact, induce deficiencies of iron, magnesium and calcium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct set of micronutrients for plants?
questions.solution: Plants require nutrients for proper growth and development. 16 elements are necessary for plants and are called essential elements as C, H, O, N, P, S, K, Mg, Ca, Fe, Cu, B, Zn, Mn, Mo, and Cl. These essential elements are categorized into 2 groups as macroelements and microelements. Macroelements are required by plants in larger amounts e.g., C, H, O, N, S, P, K, Ca, and Mg. Microelements or trace elements are required by plants in very small amounts i.e. in traces e.g., Fe, Cu, B, Mn, Mo, and Cl.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The enzyme nitrogenase is
options: Essential to convert NH<sub>3</sub> to N<sub>2</sub>
questions.solution:
The enzyme complex nitrogenase consists of two subunits:

(i) A non-heme iron protein commonly called Fe protein (or dinitrogen reductase, component I).

(ii) An iron-molybdenum protein called MoFe protein (or dinitrogenase, component II).

It is found in prokaryotes only and functions under anaerobic conditions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following sets of elements delays flowering if their concentration in plants is low?
questions.solution: Elements like N, S and Mo are necessary to promote flowering in plants. If their concentration decreases below the critical level, they delay the process of flowering.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is correctly paired?
options: Zn<sup>+2</sup> - It is an activator of nitrogenase during nitrogen fixation.
Mg<sup>+2</sup> - Activator of phosphoenol pyruvate carboxylase.
questions.solution: Mg<sup>2+</sup> is an activator for both ribulose bisphosphate carboxylaseoxygenase and phosphoenol pyruvate carboxylase, both of which are critical enzymes in photosynthetic carbon fixation; Zn<sup>2+</sup> is an activator of alcohol dehydrogenase and Mo of nitrogenase during nitrogen metabolism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Zinc is required for synthesis of
questions.solution:
Plants obtain zinc as Zn2+ ions. It activates various enzymes,
especially carboxylases. It is also needed in the synthesis of auxin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The macronutrient which is an essential component of cell organic compounds, yet not obtained by plants from soil, is
questions.solution: Carbon, oxygen, and hydrogen are called the framework elements as all the components of a living organism contain C, H and O, particularly the carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids. The three elements are taken up by the plant in the form of CO<sub>2</sub> and H<sub>2</sub>O.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A particular mineral element P activates various enzymes, especially nitrate reductase. Identify P.
questions.solution: Plants obtain Mo in the form of molybdate ions (MoO<sub>2</sub><sup>2+</sup>). It is a component of several enzymes, including nitrogenase and nitrate reductase, both of which participate in nitrogen metabolism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Mark out the number of incorrect statement/s:

[I] Some essential elements can alter the osmotic potential of a cell.
[II] Nitrogen is required by the meristematic tissues and the metabolically active cells only.
[III] Mg+2 is needed by several respiratory enzymes.
[IV] Mo is essential for the water-splitting reaction in photosynthesis, a reaction that leads to oxygen evolution.
[V] Sulphur is the main constituent of several coenzymes, vitamins (thiamine, biotin, coenzyme-A) and ferredoxin.
questions.solution: Statement II and IV are incorrect. Mn is essential for water splitting and Nitrogen is needed by all the cells. Nitrogen is required by all parts of a plant, particularly the meristematic tissues and the metabolically active cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The role of molybdenum is:
questions.solution: Molybdenum is essential for the functioning of enzyme nitrogenase in the leguminous plants for metabolising nitrogen and thus, it helps in biological nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plants deficient in elemental nitrogen, often show its effect on the biosynthesis of:
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Nitrogen is the essential nutrient element required by plants in the greatest amount. It is absorbed mainly as NO<sub>3</sub><sup>–</sup>, though some are also taken up as NO<sub>2</sub><sup>– </sup>or NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>. Nitrogen is required by all parts of a plant, particularly the meristematic tissues and the metabolically active cells. Nitrogen is one of the major constituents of proteins, nucleic acids, vitamins and hormones.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following elements in plants is not remobilised?
questions.solution: Elements such as sulphur and calcium are a part of the structural component of the cell and hence, are not easily released. This aspect of mineral nutrition of plants is of great significance and importance to agriculture and horticulture.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Nitrosomonas and Nitrococcus are associated with which of the following reaction?
questions.solution: In nitrification, ammonia is first converted to nitrites (NO2-) and then to nitrates. The initial step of this process is carried out by Nitrosomonas, and then nitrite is oxidized to nitrate by the action of Nitrococcus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A small aquatic plant was put in each of the petri dishes X and Y containing different culture solutions. After six weeks, the plant in dish X had the same number of leaves as earlier, and all leaves were small and yellowish. The plant in dish Y had more leaves of normal size and dark green colour. Which of the following set of elements would be missing in the culture of dish X?
questions.solution: The types of deficiency symptoms shown in plants include chlorosis, necrosis, stunted plant growth, premature fall of leaves and buds and inhibition of cell division. Chlorosis is the loss of chlorophyll leading to yellowing in leaves. This symptom is caused by the deficiency of elements N, K, Mg, S, Fe, Mn, Zn and Mo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The function of which cell organelle is affected the most due to the deficiency of magnesium?
questions.solution: Magnesium ion is very much necessary for the formation and functioning of the ribosome. Two ribosomal subunits bind to form complete ribosome only in presence of magnesium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The process of nitrogen cycling by microbes involves multiple steps of oxidation and simultaneous reduction. The following reaction occurring during one such step is brought about by which bacteria?
questions.solution: The reaction is the oxidation of nitrite into nitrate. This reaction is catalyzed by the bacteria Nitrobacter. Nitrosomonas and Nitrococcus are responsible for the Ammonia to nitrite. Thiobacillus and Pseudomonas are responsible for denitrification.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following element is required in minor quantities for the growth of plants but is extremely important for growth of animals?
questions.solution: Certain elements required in very small quantities are called microelements or trace elements. Sodium (Na) is one such element that is required in very small quantities and is not as important for the growth of plants as it is for animals.

Match the following and choose the correct combination from given options.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find the odd one out with respect to micronutrients.
questions.solution: Calcium is a macronutrient required by plant in large quantity. Mn, B and Cu are micronutrients required by plant in less quantity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following elements is required in the synthesis of plant growth hormones such as auxin?
questions.solution: Plants obtain zinc as Zn<sup>2+</sup> ions. It activates various enzymes, especially carboxylases. It is also needed in the synthesis of auxin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
From the following, how many amino acids contain sulphur in their chemical structure?

Methionine, histidine, threonine, cysteine, alanine, tryptophan, valine
questions.solution: Sulphur is an essential element as it is required for amino acid synthesis and hence extremely crucial for protein synthesis. The amino acids methionine and cysteine are the two which contain sulphur. Sulphur is also important as it forms a part of many coenzymes and vitamins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following.
 
  Column-I (Mineral)   Column-II (Role)
a. K (i) Water splitting
b. Zn (ii) Energy metabolism
c. Mg (iii) Auxin synthesis
d. Mn (iv) Stomatal movement
questions.solution: K = Stomatal movement (Potassium is involved in protein synthesis, opening, and closing of stomata); Zn = Auxin synthesis (Zinc is required in the synthesis of auxin); Mg = Energy metabolism (Magnesium activates the enzymes of respiration and photosynthesis); Mn = Water splitting (Splitting of water molecule during photosynthesis is facilitated by manganese).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A micronutrient is the one which is
options: More important than any major elements and are boron (B), chlorine (Cl), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), magnesium (Mg), molybdenum (Mo), and zinc (Zn).
Less important than major elements and are boron (B), chlorine (Cl), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), molybdenum (Mo), and zinc (Zn) and phosphorous (P)
Needed in small quantity but is as important as a major element and are boron (B), chlorine (Cl), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), molybdenum (Mo), and zinc (Zn).
Found small quantities in the soil and are boron (B), chlorine (Cl), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), magnesium (Mg), molybdenum (Mo), and zinc (Zn) and calcium (Ca).
questions.solution: Essential elements required in large quantities are called macro and those required in small quantities are called micronutrient. Essential elements are very much necessary for normal growth and reproduction of the plant, they participate directly in the metabolic reaction, and their deficiency results in deficiency symptoms. The important microelements are boron (B), chlorine (Cl), copper (Cu), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), molybdenum (Mo), and zinc (Zn).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A free-living, anaerobic, nitrogen-fixing bacterium is
questions.solution: Rhizobium can carry out nitrogen fixation only in a symbiotic state when it forms root nodules with leguminous plants. Azotobacter is a free-living aerobic nitrogen fixer and Clostridium is a free-living anaerobic nitrogen fixer. Streptococcus is saprophytic bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify the nutrients that are required.

A: This nutrient helps in the utilization of calcium.
B: This nutrient is the component of the nitrate reductase enzyme.
C: This nutrient is required for the photolysis of water.
options: A: Cu; B: Zn; C: Cl
A: Zn; B: Mo; C: Cl
A: B; B: Mo; C: Mn
A: Fe; B: Cu; C: Mn
questions.solution:
Boron: Boron is required for uptake and utilisation of Ca2+, membrane functioning, pollen germination, cell elongation, cell differentiation and carbohydrate translocation.

Molybdenum: It is a component of several enzymes, including nitrogenase and nitrate reductase both of which participate in nitrogen metabolism.

Manganese: It activates many enzymes involved in photosynthesis, respiration, and nitrogen metabolism. The best-defined function of manganese is in the splitting of water to liberate oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In plant nutrition, elements are classified as major or minor depending on
options: Their relative production in the ash obtained after burning the plants
The relative amounts required by the plants
Their relative importance in plant growth
questions.solution: Major elements are required by plants in the quantity of more than 1 milligram/gram of dry matter, and minor elements are required in the quantity of less than 1 milligram/gram of dry matter.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Leg-haemoglobin is found in the nodules in roots of leguminous plants. It acts as .......... scavenger and provides............ conditions for the action of nitrogenase enzyme.
questions.solution:
Enzyme nitrogenase: It is a Mo–Fe protein. It requires anaerobic conditions to work. It is highly sensitive to molecular oxygen. It catalyzes the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia. Ammonia is the first stable product of nitrogen fixation.

N2 + 8e- + 8H+ + 16ATP → 2NH3 + H2 + 16ADP + 16Pi

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the role of Pseudomonas in the soil?
questions.solution: Ammonia is oxidized to nitrite by the bacteria Nitrosomonas and Nitrococcus. The nitrite is further oxidized to nitrate with the help of the bacterium Nitrobacter. These steps are called nitrification. Nitrate present in the soil is also reduced to nitrogen by the process of denitrification, which is carried by bacteria Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus.

B. Mo 2. Delayed flowering
C. Fe 3. Necrosis
D. Cl 4. Photolysis of water
questions.solution:
Calcium is required by the meristematic and differentiating tissues for cell wall formation as it is an important component of middle lamella as calcium pectate. It is also needed during for synthesis of the mitotic spindle. Necrosis refers to the death of tissues resulting in the deficiency of elements like calcium, magnesium, copper, potassium.

Delayed flowering results in the deficiency of elements like nitrogen, sulfur and molybdenum. Molybdenum is a component of various enzymes like nitrogenase and nitrate reductase (both involved in nitrogen metabolism). 

Chlorine is absorbed along with  Na+ and  K+. It also determines the solute concentration and the anion–cation balance in cells. Mn, Cl and Ca are involved in the photolysis of water leading to oxygen evolution.

Iron is an important constituent of ferredoxin and cytochromes (proteins involved in the transfer of electrons). It is required in larger amounts in comparison to the other micronutrients. Chlorosis is the loss of chlorophyll leading to yellowing of leaves. Deficiency of elements nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, sulfur, iron, manganese, zinc and molybdenum causes chlorosis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In leguminous plants, there exists a symbiotic association between the plant and the bacterium. Choose the correct statement regarding this.
options: The bacteria derive reduced  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  from plant
The bacteria supply reduced <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> to the plant and receive sugars from plant
The nodule is produced by the plant independent of bacteria
The plant growth is inhibited by the factors produced by bacteria
questions.solution: Legumes form a unique symbiotic relationship with bacteria known as Rhizobium, which they allow to infect their roots. This leads to root nodule formation where bacteria are accommodated to convert nitrogen from the air into ammonia that the plant can use for growth. In turn, bacteria receive food from the plants in the form of sugars.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Cadmium is not an essential element for plants. Phosphorus is macronutrient, iron and manganese are micronutrients required by plants for growth.

questions.subject: Botany

II. Mn competes with iron and magnesium for uptake.

questions.solution: Manganese is absorbed in the form of manganous ions. It activates many enzymes involved in photosynthesis, respiration and nitrogen metabolism. It is involved in photolysis of water during non-cyclic photophosphorylation to liberate oxygen during photosynthesis. Manganese competes with iron and magnesium for uptake and with magnesium for binding with enzymes. Manganese inhibits calcium translocation in shoot apex.

questions.solution: Free living nitrogen fixing aerobic microbes are Azobacter and Beijerinckia while Rhodospirillum is anaerobic and free living. Cyanobacteria such as Nostoc are also free living nitrogen fixers. Rhizobium has a symbiotic relationship with roots of legumes like, pea, lentils, alfalfa etc. They produce nodules on the roots. Similar to this is Frankia which also produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of non-leguminous plant Alnus. Ammonia is first oxidised to nitrite by the bacteria Nitrosomonas and/or Nitrococcus. The nitrite is further oxidised to nitrate with the help of the bacterium Nitrobacter. These steps are called nitrification.

questions.q: What is the correct fate of ammonium ions in plants?
options: It undergoes transamination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to form glumate acid which further undergoes reductive amination to form other amino acids
It undergoes reductive amination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to glumatine which further undergoes transamination to form other amino acids
It undergoes transamination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to glumatine which further undergoes reductive amination to form other amino acids
It undergoes reductive amination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to glumate which further undergoes transamination to form other amino acids
questions.solution:
At physiological pH, the ammonia is protonated to form (ammonium) ion.

(i) Reductive amination : In these processes, ammonium ion reacts with α-ketoglutaric acid and forms glutamic acid. (ii) Transamination : It involves the transfer of amino group from one amino acid to the keto group of a keto acid. Glutamic acid is the main amino acid from which the transfer of NH2, the amino group takes place and other amino acids are formed through transamination. The enzyme transaminase catalyses all such reactions.

options: It can avoid problem of soil borne pathogens
Out of season vegetables and flowers can be obtained
questions.solution:
The growing of plants with their roots in dilute solutions of mineral salts instead of soil led to increased understanding of plant nutrition. This cultivation of plants by placing the roots in nutrient solution is called hydroponics.

Hydroponics is a subset of hydroculture and is a method of growing plants using mineral nutrient solutions, in water, without soil. Terrestrial plants may be grown with their roots in the mineral nutrient solution only or in an inert medium, such as perlite or gravel.

It can avoid problem of soil borne pathogens. It avoids problem of weeding. Out of season vegetables and flowers can be obtained through hydroponics.

(iii) Fixation of nitrogen in legumes
(iv) Conversion from ammonium to nitrate in soil
questions.solution: The process by which N<sub>2</sub> is reduced to NH<sup>4+</sup> is called nitrogen fixation. Nitrogenase enzyme catalyzes this reduction. It is only carried out by prokaryotic microorganisms. Principle N<sub>2</sub>-fixers include certain free-living cyanobacteria in symbiotic associations with fungi lichens or with ferns, mosses, and liverworts, and by bacteria or other microbes associated symbiotically with roots, especially those of legumes. About 15 percent of the nearly 20,000 species in the Fabaceae (leguminosae) family have been examined for N<sub>2</sub> fixation, and approximately 90 percent of these have root nodules in which fixation occurs. So without active nitrogenase enzyme, there will be no N<sub>2</sub> fixation in legumes.

This pigment is responsible for absorbing the light energy and convert into chemical energy to be used in making glucose. questions.solution: Several types of symbiotic biological nitrogen fixing associations are known. The most prominent among them is the legume-bacteria relationship. Species of rod-shaped Rhizobium has such relationship with the roots of several legumes such as alfalfa, sweet clover, sweet pea, lentils, garden pea, broad bean, clover beans, etc. The most common association on roots is as nodules. questions.solution:
Magnesium is a structural component of chlorophyll. A chlorophyll molecule consists of a single magnesium atom present in the center which is attached to four pyrrole rings. Iron is a functional component for the synthesis of chlorophyll.
The chlorophyll molecule is made up of a squarish tetrapyrrolic ring known as head and phytol alcohol called the tail. The magnesium atom is present in the central position of the tetrapyrrolic ring. The four pyrrole rings of porphyrin head are linked together by methine (CH =) groups forming a ring system.

When central Mg is replaced by Fe, the chlorophyll becomes a green pigment called 'cytochrome' which is used in photosynthesis (Photophosphorylation) and respiration both.

Nitrogen is one of the essential macronutrients required by plants and absorbed in the form of nitrates and nitrites. It forms a major constituent of proteins, vitamins, chlorophyll, pyrimidines and hormones. Deficiency of nitrogen of leads to stunted growth, chlorosis, reduced cell division, decrease in protein content, wrinkling of cereal grains, purple coloration of the shoot axis.

Iron is another essential element necessary for plant growth and development. Chlorophyll production requires iron and it is a component of many enzymes which participate in energy transfer, nitrogen fixation, lignification. Iron deficiency is clearly indicated by chlorosis where leaf yellowing appears first in the interveinal regions of the young leaves. Chlorosis referes to production of insufficienct chlorophyll leading to yellowing of the leaves.

Chlorine is absorbed in the form of chloride ions and it helps in maintaining salt balance in cells of plant. Chlorine is important for opening and closing of stomata. Chlorine deficiency results in the wilting of the leaves which later turn in bronze colour.

Boron is another essential element which is required for membrane functioning, pollen germination, cell differentiation. It is also required for calcium uptake and utilization. Boron deficiency symptoms include leaves with yellowish or reddish cast, growing points stop functioning leading to stunted or rosette appearance. Its deficiency also causes formation of cracked fruits.

questions.q: Which of the following mineral elements is needed during the formation of the mitotic spindle, which accumulates in older leaves, and is involved in the normal functioning of the cell membrane?
questions.solution: Calcium is necessary for the formation of spindle fiber during mitosis. It is an immobile element and is accumulated in older leaves and is involved in the normal functioning of the cell membrane. It is necessary for the formation of the middle lamella of plants where it occurs as calcium pectate. It is necessary for the growth of apical meristem and root hair formation. It acts as an activator of several enzymes, e.g., ATPase, succinic dehydrogenase, adenylate kinase, etc. Along with Na+ and K+ it maintains the permeability of plasma membrane.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a nitrogen fixing organism?
questions.solution: Certain prokaryotic organisms are capable fixing nitrogen available in the air and reduce it to ammonia. They have presence of an enzyme called nitrogenase which helps in reduction of nitrogen to ammonia. This process is called biological nitrogen fixation and the organisms are called nitrogen fixers. These nitrogen fixers could be free living or symbiotic. The examples of these free living microbes are Azotobacter, Rhodospirillum, Anabaena, Nostoc, etc. Pseudomonas are not nitrogen fixing bacterias.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mark the incorrect option w.r.t. nitrifying bacteria
questions.solution:
Ammonia is first oxidised to nitrite by the bacteria Nitrosomonas and/or Nitrococcus. The nitrite is further oxidised to nitrate with the help of the bacterium Nitrobacter. These steps are called nitrification.

These nitrifying bacteria are chemoautotrophs. The nitrate thus formed is absorbed by plants and is transported to the leaves. In leaves, it is reduced to form ammonia that finally forms the amine group of amino acids. Nitrate present in the soil is also reduced to nitrogen by the process of denitrification. Denitrification is carried by bacteria Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus.
